children: Australia's stronger-than-expected inflation result for October is an uncomfortable reminder that the country's problem with price pressures continues, says Cherelle Murphy, chief economist at EY. Murphy still expects the Reserve Bank of Australia to leave rates on hold in December, but adds that it's harder after this inflation read to rule out another hike next year. Most concerning for the RBA, underlying inflation accelerated to 3.8% on year, compared with 3.6% previously, suggesting inflation momentum is remaining stubbornly strong, she adds.
